reasons: B consists only of the oath instruction, which appears almost word for word as the closing clause of A.
Both are addressed by the Prophet to Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura ('قال لي'), so the setting matches as well as the wording.
A adds a preceding instruction about not asking for command (al-imara), which B lacks.

evidence.quote: وإذا حلفت على يمين فرأيت غيرها خيرا منها، فأت الذي هو خير، وكفر عن يمينك
إذا حلفت على يمين فرأيت غيرها خيرا منها فأت الذي هو خير وكفر عن يمينك

verdicts.uncertainty_note: Could also be read as same_report_variant (B abridged from the fuller telling); the outcome would not change.

proposals.text: A opens with the instruction not to ask for command (لا تسأل الإمارة) and its rationale; B carries only the oath clause.

reasons: Both report that the Messenger of God cursed al-wasila and al-mustawsila, in the same words.
A adds al-washima and al-mustawshima; B adds an explanatory gloss.
In both the curse is attributed to the Prophet; in B it is relayed by Abu Abd Allah, which is a matter of transmission rather than a different speaker of the ruling.

evidence.quote: لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الواصلة والمستوصلة والواشمة والمستوشمة
لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله الواصلة والمستوصلة يعني الزانية والقوادة

verdicts.uncertainty_note: The gloss in B gives the two terms a very different sense from their plain meaning (hair-joining). A reader who treats the gloss as defining the content of the report could judge this contested; I treat the shared core sentence as decisive.

proposals.text: B glosses al-wasila and al-mustawsila as 'the adulteress and the procuress' (يعني الزانية والقوادة); A gives no gloss.
A adds the woman who tattoos and the woman who asks to be tattooed (الواشمة والمستوشمة), absent from B.

reasons: A is a long account of Abu Musa correcting a man after prayer and relaying the Prophet's sermon on following the imam; the tashahhud appears only at its end.
B is a short report that the Prophet taught the tashahhud of prayer and of need, quoting the tashahhud.
The only overlap is the tashahhud formula, and even its opening wording differs between the two.

evidence.quote: فليكن من أول قول أحدكم التحيات الطيبات الصلوات لله السلام عليك أيها النبي
التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات السلام عليك أيها النبي
إذا صليتم فأقيموا صفوفكم ثم ليؤمكم أحدكم
علمنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم التشهد في الصلاة والتشهد في الحاجة

verdicts.uncertainty_note: If the claim were only that both preserve a telling of the Prophet's tashahhud teaching, one could call it a shared passage; but the narrative content, setting and formula wording differ.

proposals.text: Tashahhud wording differs: A 'التحيات الطيبات الصلوات لله', B 'التحيات لله والصلوات والطيبات'.
B also mentions a tashahhud of need (التشهد في الحاجة), which A does not.

reasons: A is mainly Ali's description of the Prophet's appearance, followed by a separately chained five-part blessing formula 'counted on the hand'.
B is only a two-part blessing formula on Muhammad, his wives and his offspring.
The overlap is the standard Abrahamic blessing frame, filled differently: A blesses 'آل محمد' with five verbs; B blesses 'أزواجه وذريته' with two.

evidence.quote: اللهم صل على محمد وعلى آل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وعلى آل إبراهيم انك حميد مجيد
اللهم صل على محمد وأزواجه وذريته كما صليت على آل إبراهيم
صف لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله كأنا ننظر إليه

verdicts.uncertainty_note: B has no chain or context in the packet; if it were shown to be the conclusion of a report about the same teaching occasion, a variant reading of the formula portion would be arguable.

proposals.text: A's formula names 'آل محمد' and adds mercy (ترحم), tenderness (تحنن) and peace (سلم) clauses; B names 'أزواجه وذريته' and has only blessing and benediction.
A combines two distinct units: a description of the Prophet (shama'il) and a chained blessing formula; only the second is near B.

reasons: Both say there is no envy except in two cases, and describe the same two men in nearly identical words.
The order of the two men is reversed, and A has 'في' where B has 'على'.

evidence.quote: لا حسد إلا في اثنتين رجل آتاه الله مالا فهو ينفق منه آناء الليل وآناء النهار
لا حسد إلا على اثنتين رجل آتاه الله القرآن فهو يقوم به آناء الليل وآناء النهار

verdicts.uncertainty_note: B carries no chain in the packet; that does not affect the matn comparison.

proposals.text: A names the man given wealth first; B names the man given the Qur'an first.

reasons: Both use the same frame 'whoever ... out of faith and seeking reward is forgiven his past sins', but fill it with different acts.
A concerns standing in prayer on Laylat al-Qadr; B concerns standing in prayer during Ramadan ('يقول لرمضان ... من قامه').

evidence.quote: من يقم ليلة القدر إيمانا واحتسابا غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه
من قامه إيمانا واحتسابا غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه

verdicts.uncertainty_note: A reader who regards these as two clauses of one longer report (which some tellings combine) could treat this as a shared passage; nothing in these two texts shows that, so I read them as distinct sayings in a common frame.

proposals.text: A's object is Laylat al-Qadr; B's object is the month of Ramadan.
